text: An explored step may declare the exception that is its refusal (#392, #396). invariant_observe.Refusal(exception_type, **attributes), a Step's keyword-only refusal, names an Exception subclass that inherits no control-flow class, and exact finite JSON scalar attributes, matched by type, by value and by a float's sign. For such a step an attempt is refused only when the entry raises exactly that exception, on its own stack or out of an async entry's awaitable, before any selected call or application thread starts, with the state read back unchanged; TLC then checks that the model disables the named step, with those arguments, in that state. A normal return is accepted only when TLC finds that the named step itself, with its arguments, relates the two states, stutters included, so another branch of Next can't justify it. Anything else fails the run. Undeclared steps keep D-0200's rule, sampled runs refuse declarations, and receipts count declared refusals apart from other refusals. CI's integration job runs the strict check's real TLC cases.
